style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The evening psalm, paired by the church with Psalm 3's morning and read since antiquity as the same crisis, the same night, the same ending in sleep. David addresses three parties in turn. First God: answer me, God of my righteousness -- You gave me room when I was hemmed in. Then the men of rank who are turning his glory into shame and chasing empty things and lies; to them he says: know that the LORD has set apart the faithful man for Himself. Tremble, and do not sin; talk it over with your own heart on your bed, and be still; offer right sacrifices and trust. Then the crowd that asks the oldest question -- who will show us any good? -- and David's answer is a prayer, Aaron's benediction turned toward heaven: lift up the light of Your face on us. The close is the psalm's whole argument: You have put more joy in my heart than they get when their grain and new wine come in, and so I will lie down and sleep at once, in peace, because You alone, LORD, make me live in safety. The man who has God's face does not need the harvest in order to sleep.

1.text: For the choir director, with stringed instruments. A psalm of David. Answer me when I call, O God of my righteousness! In the tight place You gave me room; be gracious to me and hear my prayer.
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach] on Neginoth [neginah -- stringed instruments], A Psalm [mizmor] of David. Hear [anah -- answer] me when I call [qara], O God [Elohim] of my righteousness [tsedek]: You have enlarged [rachab -- made room for] me when I was in distress [tsar -- the narrows]; have mercy ['be gracious unto me', chanan, the KJV margin] upon me, and hear [shama] my prayer [tephillah].
1.notes: Elohe tsidqi (H430, H6664) -- the God of my righteousness: not David's own but the vindication God supplies. ba-tsar hirchavta li (H6862, H7337): in the narrows You made room -- Psalm 118:5's geometry, remembered as past tense and prayed forward: do it again, chanan (H2603), be gracious.

2.text: You men of rank, how long will you turn my glory into shame? How long will you love what is empty and chase after lies? Selah.
2.amp: O ye sons [ben] of men [ish -- men of rank], how long [ad] will ye turn my glory [kabod] into shame [kelimmah]? how long will ye love [ahab] vanity [riq -- emptiness], and seek [baqash] after leasing [kazab -- falsehood]? Selah.
2.notes: bene ish (H1121, H376) -- sons of MEN of rank, the nobility, not bene adam, the sons of Adam, mankind at large (the KJV's own 'high' against 'low' in Psalm 49:2). Their two sins: kebodi li-khlimmah (H3519, H3639), David's honor made a disgrace, and the love of riq and kazab (H7385, H3577), the empty and the false -- Absalom's propaganda, or any court's.

3.text: But know this: the LORD has set apart the faithful one for Himself; the LORD hears when I call to Him.
3.amp: But know [yada] that the LORD [YHWH] has set apart [palah -- distinguished, marked out] him that is godly [chasid -- the covenant-faithful] for Himself: the LORD will hear [shama] when I call [qara] unto Him.
3.notes: u-deu (H3045), know it: hiphlah YHWH chasid lo (H6395, H2623) -- the LORD has marked out His faithful one for Himself, palah being the verb of the plagues that distinguished Goshen from Egypt (cf. Exodus 8:22). The slanderers' opinion of David is not the one that counts.

4.text: Tremble, and do not sin; speak with your own heart on your bed, and be still. Selah.
4.amp: Stand in awe [ragaz -- tremble, be agitated], and sin [chata] not: commune [amar -- speak] with your own heart [lebab] upon your bed [mishkab], and be still [damam]. Selah.
4.notes: rigzu ve-al-techetau (H7264, H2398): tremble -- let the agitation happen -- and do not let it become sin; Paul quotes the Greek of this line as 'be angry and sin not' (cf. Ephesians 4:26). The prescription is the bedtime examination: imru bi-lebabkhem al-mishkabkhem ve-dommu (H559, H3824, H4904, H1826) -- talk it over with your heart on your bed, then be quiet.

5.text: Offer sacrifices of righteousness, and put your trust in the LORD.
5.amp: Offer [zabach] the sacrifices [zebach] of righteousness [tsedek], and put your trust [batach] in the LORD [YHWH].
5.notes: zibchu zibche-tsedek (H2076, H2077, H6664): right sacrifices -- offered rightly, from right hearts -- not the ritual cover of the rebels who sacrificed at Hebron to bless a coup (cf. 2 Samuel 15:12). And bitchu el-YHWH (H982): the trust that makes a sacrifice mean something.

6.text: Many are saying, 'Who will show us anything good?' Lift up the light of Your face upon us, O LORD!
6.amp: There be many [rav] that say [amar], Who will show [raah] us any good [tov]? LORD [YHWH], lift up [nasa] the light [or] of Your countenance [panim] upon us.
6.notes: The crowd's question, mi-yarenu tov (H7200, H2896) -- who will show us anything good? -- the perennial cynicism of a bad season. David answers with Aaron's blessing prayed upward: nesah-alenu or panekha (H5375, H216, H6440), lift the light of Your face over us (cf. Numbers 6:25-26). The good they are looking for has a face.

7.text: You have put more gladness in my heart than they have when their grain and their new wine abound.
7.amp: You have put [natan] gladness [simchah] in my heart [leb], more than in the time [et] that their corn [dagan -- grain] and their wine [tirosh -- new wine] increased [rabab].
7.notes: natatta simchah be-libbi (H5414, H8057, H3820): gladness put in, deposited, by God -- me-et deganam ve-tirosham rabbu (H6256, H1715, H8492, H7231), more than harvest-joy, the loudest joy an agrarian world knew. The comparison is the psalm's thesis: God's face outweighs a good year.

8.text: In peace I will lie down and sleep at once, for You alone, O LORD, let me dwell in safety.
8.amp: I will both [yachad -- at once, together] lay me down [shakab] in peace [shalom], and sleep [yashen]: for You, LORD [YHWH], only [badad -- alone] make me dwell [yashab] in safety [betach].
8.notes: be-shalom yachdav eshkevah ve-ishan (H7965, H3162, H7901, H3462) -- 'at once': lie down and sleep in one motion, no tossing. ki-attah YHWH le-badad (H910) -- You alone (the Hebrew can also attach 'alone' to the dwelling, as in Deuteronomy 33:28: a solitary safety only God gives) -- la-betach toshiveni (H983, H3427): safety as a dwelling God settles a man into. The church's bedtime psalm at Compline, its night office, for fifteen centuries, and Psalm 3:5's morning claim made from the other end of the night.
